text:
leah_sales: Quick sync - enterprise customer (regulated payments) wants a Private Deploy POC next sprint. Requirements: PrivateLink for isolation, cross-AZ HA, on-prem fallback over TGW/BGP, and monthly EIP rotation for compliance. They also want to keep client source IPs in our auth logs. Can we outline network constraints + a short ops handoff they can give to their netops team?

ian_netops: TL;DR: PrivateLink = interface endpoints (ENIs) that terminate in the VPC and NAT traffic -> you lose original source IP. Options to preserve identity: 1) egress proxy in-customer-VPC that forwards X-Forwarded-For / adds proxied header; 2) use a TCP proxy with PROXY protocol so backend sees client IP; 3) run traffic through TGW/NAT appliance with BYOIP so traffic source is preserved end-to-end. Each has tradeoffs (latency, ops, TLS inspection).

maria_arch: Adding infra details: for AZ HA create 1 endpoint per AZ + a small HA proxy fleet behind them (autoscale minimal). For cross-region either duplicate endpoints or use inter-region TGW. BGP fallback pattern: prefer route to interface endpoints (local target), then learned BGP route advertised to TGW as lower-priority failover. I can attach a sample BGP policy next.

owen_security: From questionnaire perspective we need: a list of endpoint FQDNs and EIP ranges, confirmation on TLS expectations (SNI vs mTLS), KMS usage for request-level logs, retention windows, and an EIP rotation plan (dates + maintenance window). If they mandate monthly EIP churn we require automation to update their firewall rules or a wildcard FQDN-based allowlist for outbound.

ian_netops: Minimal firewall snippet for their ops (customer egress rules):
```
# allow egress to Redwood POC endpoints
ALLOW TCP 10.12.0.0/16 -> 52.45.123.77/32 443
# if using interface endpoints, allow to VPC endpoint ENIs
ALLOW TCP 10.12.0.0/16 -> vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f 443
# healthchecks from our probe CIDR
ALLOW TCP 10.12.0.0/16 <- 15.60.200.0/24 443
```
Replace IPs/IDs with values in POC ticket. Note: if their proxy rewrites SNI, recommend mTLS or PROXY protocol to avoid cert mismatch.

maria_arch: Cost guidance for sales: PrivateLink incurs per-endpoint hourly + per-GB data processing cost. VPC peering/TGW avoids per-endpoint charge but may incur transit data costs and more customer infra. For a short POC (<2TB/mo) PrivateLink is usually simplest; for sustained multi-TB traffic peering+TGW or Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity could be cheaper. I can model cost if you give expected egress GB / sustained RPS.

leah_sales: Can someone paste a 3-line handoff (network ops) and a 2-line security checklist (info sec) I can drop into the customer's ticket? Deadline: they want the handoff by EOD.

owen_security: 2-line security checklist for their infosec: 
- Provide KMS policy + CIEM scan results; confirm TLS requirements (mTLS preferred for endpoints).
- Agree maintenance windows for monthly EIP rotation; provide automation plan for firewall updates or accept FQDN allowlist.

ian_netops: 3-line network ops handoff: 
- Deploy PrivateLink interface endpoints in each AZ for POC; configure HA proxies to load-balance across endpoint ENIs.
- Note PrivateLink NATs client IP; if original src IP is required use an in-VPC egress proxy that sets X-Forwarded-For or enable PROXY protocol to backend.
- Open outbound TCP/443 to assigned EIP(s) or vpce IDs; expect per-endpoint hourly + per-GB charges; if rotating EIPs monthly, schedule maintenance windows and automate firewall rule updates.

handshake_bot: handshake-bot: Created ticket POC-9002-network-handoff and assigned to #eng-infra and #eng-platform — ETA 4 business days.

maria_arch: Blockers before POC: their network diagram, expected monthly egress (GB), RPS peak, and whether they will inspect TLS (SNI rewrite) or allow passthrough. If they supply those we can spin test endpoints in 48h.

leah_sales: I'll collect the diagram + traffic estimate and paste into POC-9002. Thanks all! :white_check_mark:
